name: Bazigar
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page bazi1237 'Bazigar' (Hammarström et al.)
sources.note: Unclassifiable; ISO bfr; only reference is Ethnologue endangerment (7 Shifting). Zero descriptive references; the four Glottolog refs in our source list are all ethnographic overviews.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority, code page bfr
sources.note: Code record only; change-request index blocked by an automated-access block.

Phonology paragraph is a second-hand paraphrase of Schreffler 2011 pp. 225–26 (Punjabi-like phonology, /ç/, no /h/, tone in place of /h/); cites Deb 1987 p. 17 for resemblance to Bagri. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul, Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2013. Ethnologue 17th ed., entry 'Bazigar' (bfr) (Internet Archive copy of 2013-03-28)
sources.note: Population 58,200 (1981 census), ethnic 800,000; locations; then classified 'Dravidian, Unclassified'; literacy <1%. No linguistic description. Current Ethnologue entry could not be reached by automated download/paywall.

sources.citation: Tyagi, Mohan (ਡਾ. ਮੋਹਨ ਤਿਆਗੀ). 2013. ਬਾਜ਼ੀਗਰ ਕਬੀਲੇ ਦਾ ਸਭਿਆਚਾਰ [Bāzīgar kabīle dā sabhiācār; Culture of the Bazigar tribe]. New Delhi: National Book Trust, India. 209 pp. (Punjabi, Gurmukhi).
sources.note: Ch. 8 'ਬਾਜ਼ੀਗਰ ਕਬੀਲੇ ਦੀ ਭਾਸ਼ਾ ਅਤੇ ਗੁਪਤ ਭਾਸ਼ਾ' (Language and secret language of the Bazigar tribe), pp. 69–77: sociolinguistic prose (language called 'Gor', of Rajasthani origin, unwritten, mixed with Gujarati/Marwari/Hindi/Braj; secret language 'Parsi'; Punjabi as contact language) and a 139-item Punjabi–Bazigar–secret-language wordlist (pp. 73–77). No phonology section; no statement on stress or tone (only that the secret language differs in 'ਉਚਾਰਣ ਲਹਿਜਾ' = pronunciation/accent, p. 71, which is not word stress). Gurmukhi scanned not possible (tesseract has eng only); pages read visually.

sources.citation: Schreffler, Gibb. 2011. The Bazigar (Goaar) People and Their Performing Arts. Journal of Punjab Studies 18(1&2): 217–250 (34 pp.). Santa Barbara: UCSB Center for Sikh and Punjab Studies.
sources.note: One 'Language' paragraph (pp. 225–226): phonology 'more or less equivalent to Punjabi', retroflex /ḷ/, an extra voiceless palatal fricative /ç/; 'The language's system of lexical tones is also like Punjabi' except that /h/ is absent and Punjabi /h/-cognates 'substitute a tone'. Nothing whatsoever on stress or accent placement. Ethnomusicological article, not a linguistic description.

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. 1922. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. XI: Gipsy Languages. Calcutta: Govt. of India.
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accent Bazigar/Bāzīgar: no hit; the LSI does not treat this variety.

sources.citation: Ibbetson, Denzil. 1916 [1883]. Panjab Castes. Lahore: Superintendent of Government Printing, Punjab. (Glottolog ref 146225, listed by Glottolog as an overview)
sources.note: Para. 588 'The Nat and Bazigar' (orig. p. 315): ethnographic only (Bazigar = Persian occupational term, acrobats/jugglers, grouped with Nat, called Badi in Delhi/Hissar). Nothing on language.

sources.citation: Shodhganga hits 7–26 for 'Bazigar' (result pages 2–3 not retrieved; possible Punjabi-medium linguistic MA/PhD thesis on ਬਾਜ਼ੀਗਰ ਬੋਲੀ at Punjabi University Patiala / GNDU)
sources.note: Only plausible place a phonological description (with stress) of Bazigar boli could exist; page 1 of the listing was all sociology/genetics, pages 2–3 unseen.
